# IDMC Endpoint Dictionary

Every endpoint in this knowledge base, in one place, answering *what is this path, which verbs actually work on it, and where do I call it*.

**Generated** by `build/build_dictionary.py` from `content/*.json` — the same source as the master document that `build/build_master.py` renders (not shipped). Do not edit this file by hand; edit the section JSON and rebuild. The master document is organised by product, for reading. This is organised by path, for lookup.

**167 endpoints** across 13 services, **11 MCP actions**, plus 28 operations that have no endpoint at all.

## How to read an entry

Four states, never merged, because conflating them is the mistake this whole document exists to prevent:

| Label | Means |
|---|---|
| **Works** | A live status code was observed on this verb. Trust it. |
| **Documented** | Informatica documents the verb; nobody exercised it here. Plausible, unproven. |
| **Rejected** | The verb was explicitly refused, with the code. A `405` is a *finding*: the resource is read-only at any permission level. |
| **Untested** | Nobody probed it. **Unknown, not unsupported.** Do not quote this as a limitation. |

A `404` with an empty body is a genuine UI-only wall. A `404` *with* a body is usually the wrong path or wrong host — keep hunting. Full decoder in the appendix.

## The Postman question, answered

Across 167 endpoints:

| Verb | Works | Documented only | Rejected | Untested |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `GET` | 83 | 7 | 35 | 41 |
| `POST` | 38 | 8 | 28 | 92 |
| `PUT` | 0 | 14 | 11 | 141 |
| `PATCH` | 0 | 5 | 9 | 152 |
| `DELETE` | 5 | 7 | 6 | 148 |

What that table means in practice:

- **`GET` and `POST` are the platform.** 83 endpoints read, 38 write or run. Everything else is a rounding error.
- **`PUT` is nearly absent and `PATCH` effectively does not exist** — 0 and 0 proven respectively. IDMC has almost no in-place edit. The sanctioned update pattern is `DELETE` then re-`POST` (`/public/core/v3/users/{id}` is canonical: `PUT` and `PATCH` both 405), or, on the v2 plane, **`POST` to the `/{id}` path — that *is* the update**.
- **`DELETE` is rare** (5 proven) and clustered in admin, connections, catalog sources and CDQ dictionaries.
- **`HEAD` and `OPTIONS` appear nowhere** in any guide or probe. There is no preflight discovery: to test whether a write verb exists, `POST` an empty body — **400 / 415 / 422 means the verb is there**, 405 means it is not.
- **65 of the 167 endpoints have no working verb** — 18 documented but never exercised, 33 explicitly marked *none proven*, and 12 whose source row names a verb but whose only evidence is a failure code, so this dictionary reports the verb as **Rejected** rather than Works. Separately, 14 operations are **UI-only with no endpoint at all**. That gap — read and run over REST, author and publish in the browser — is the single most important shape of this platform.

## Migration - export & import

*Last verified 2026-07-26.*

### `/public/core/v3/export`

Start an export job for named objects

**Works:** POST · **Rejected:** GET 405 · **Untested:** PUT, PATCH, DELETE

*Plane:* v3 platform — `<pod>.dm-us.informaticacloud.com/saas` · header `INFA-SESSION-ID`

*Evidence:* 200 on submission. Empty objects[] -> 400. TWO DISTINCT 400s worth telling apart, live 2026-07-26: MigrationSvc_041 'No asset selected for export operation' means the body shape was ACCEPTED but the named object contributes no exportable asset (e.g. an empty Project) - it is a CONTENT verdict, not a shape error; V3API_007 'Bad Request' means the body shape itself is wrong. objects[] takes OBJECTS ({"id": "..."}), never bare id strings, and adding a 'type' key produces V3API_007.

### `/public/core/v3/export/{id}`

Export job status

**Works:** GET · **Untested:** POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE

*Evidence:* 200

### `/public/core/v3/export/{id}/package`

Download the round-trippable .zip

**Works:** GET · **Untested:** POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE

*Plane:* v3 platform — `<pod>.dm-us.informaticacloud.com/saas` · header `INFA-SESSION-ID`

*Evidence:* 200

### `/public/core/v3/import`

Bare import

**Works:** none proven · **Rejected:** POST 404 · **Untested:** GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE

*Plane:* v3 platform — `<pod>.dm-us.informaticacloud.com/saas` · header `INFA-SESSION-ID`

*Evidence:* 404 No static resource core/v3/import

### `/public/core/v3/import/package`

Import a GENUINE export zip

**Works:** POST · **Untested:** GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE

*Plane:* v3 platform — `<pod>.dm-us.informaticacloud.com/saas` · header `INFA-SESSION-ID`

*Evidence:* 200 on a genuine package. THE TRAP IS CONTENT-TYPE, verified live 2026-07-26 across four encodings on one org: application/json -> 404 MigrationSvc_025 'Import request with identifier [package] doesnt exist' (reads as a DEAD ROUTE and is not - the service is parsing 'package' as an importId); application/zip -> 415; application/octet-stream -> 415; multipart/form-data -> 400 MigrationSvc_030 'Invalid import package' = the handler parsed the upload and rejected the CONTENT. So MigrationSvc_030 is the SUCCESS signal for route discovery and only means the zip was hand-built. Send multipart/form-data with a genuine export zip.

### `/public/core/v3/import/upload`

Upload a package

**Works:** none proven · **Rejected:** POST · **Untested:** GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE

*Plane:* v3 platform — `<pod>.dm-us.informaticacloud.com/saas` · header `INFA-SESSION-ID`

*Evidence:* 415 Unsupported Media Type on application/json, and 404 MigrationSvc_025 'Import request with identifier [upload] doesnt exist' - i.e. the segment after /import/ is read as an importId, so this is not a separate upload route. The real path is /public/core/v3/import/package with multipart/form-data.

### `/public/core/v3/import/{jobId}`

Import job status

**Works:** GET · **Untested:** POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE

*Plane:* v3 platform — `<pod>.dm-us.informaticacloud.com/saas` · header `INFA-SESSION-ID`

*Evidence:* 200

**MCP coverage:** No MCP server covers this service. Everything here is REST-only.

> **A 404 that names your path segment is not a dead route.** MigrationSvc_025 'Import request with identifier [X] doesnt exist' means the service read X as an importId and looked it up. That is a live handler answering a lookup, not a missing route - and because it is a 404 it is very easy to file under Law 3 as 'wrong path' and walk away. Before concluding a write route is absent, vary the CONTENT-TYPE as well as the path: on this endpoint json gives 404, zip and octet-stream give 415, and only multipart reaches the validator.

> **MigrationSvc_041 vs V3API_007 - a content verdict is not a shape error.** On /v3/export, MigrationSvc_041 'No asset selected' means your body parsed fine and the target simply holds nothing exportable; V3API_007 means the body shape is wrong. Reading 041 as a shape error sends you sweeping body variants against an endpoint that already accepted your request - the fix is to pick a different object, not a different body.

> ⚠️ **Open question.** Whether the multipart field name matters. 'package' was used and reached MigrationSvc_030; no other field name was tried, so a cleaner 200 path may exist.

**MCP coverage:** No MCP server covers this service. Everything here is REST-only.

#### Caps that bite here

- **Bulk publish / unpublish** — 199 assets per call *(Invoke ch.3-4)*
- **Process list default page size** — 20 (use listStart + maxReturn to page) *(Monitor p.101)*
- **Rate limit** — HTTP 429 when requests exceed the window *(Invoke p.12)*
- **Activity execution circuit breaker** — 10,000 activities -> 429, no new instances for 15 min (tech preview, node-local) *(Invoke p.25)*
- **Message payload** — 5 MB on Cloud Server; 500 MB multi-byte ceiling *(Monitor p.11)*
- **Process timeout / retention** — 3,600 s timeout; completed 24 h, faulted 72 h, logs 30 days *(Invoke p.25)*
- **Bulk publish / unpublish** — 199 assets per call, processed in payload order *(Invoke pp.30, 32)*
- **Unpublish dependency order** — Service connector, THEN app connection, THEN process. Wrong order returns per-item ERROR inside a 200 envelope. *(Invoke p.35)*
- **REST / SOAP rate limit** — HTTP 429 once the rate limit is exceeded in the window *(Invoke p.12)*
- **Invocable verbs** — GET, POST, PATCH, PUT, DELETE on a published process *(Invoke p.15)*

- **Bulk publish / unpublish** — 199 assets per call *(Invoke ch.3-4)*

- **Rate limit** — HTTP 429 when requests exceed the window *(Invoke p.12)*
- **Activity execution circuit breaker** — 10,000 activities -> 429, no new instances for 15 min (tech preview, node-local) *(Invoke p.25)*
- **Message payload** — 5 MB on Cloud Server; 500 MB multi-byte ceiling *(Monitor p.11)*
- **Process timeout / retention** — 3,600 s timeout; completed 24 h, faulted 72 h, logs 30 days *(Invoke p.25)*
- **Bulk publish / unpublish** — 199 assets per call, processed in payload order *(Invoke pp.30, 32)*
- **Unpublish dependency order** — Service connector, THEN app connection, THEN process. Wrong order returns per-item ERROR inside a 200 envelope. *(Invoke p.35)*
- **REST / SOAP rate limit** — HTTP 429 once the rate limit is exceeded in the window *(Invoke p.12)*
- **Invocable verbs** — GET, POST, PATCH, PUT, DELETE on a published process *(Invoke p.15)*

Ingestion job status

**Works:** none proven · **Documented:** GET · **Untested:** POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE

*Plane:* Ingestion (DBMI) — `<pod>-ing.dm-us.informaticacloud.com` · header `Bearer + IDS-SESSION-ID`

*Evidence:* LIVE 2026-07-26: THE 404s WERE A WRONG-HOST ERROR. DBMI is served on a dedicated <pod>-ing.<domain> host, NOT the pod/saas host. Proven with controls: <pod>-ing resolves (a public A record) while <pod>-bogusZZZ has no DNS, and the SAME path returns a bare 404 on the pod host but a real DBMI error envelope on -ing. Consistently 415 'Content-Type is not supported' on GET, with and without query params, and 405 on POST. 415 means the route is LIVE and content-negotiating - it is rejecting our media type, not the path. Unresolved: which Content-Type/Accept it wants (stripping our headers did not clear it). Real progress vs the previous bare 404.

Proven with controls: <pod>-ing resolves (a public A record) while <pod>-bogusZZZ has no DNS, and the SAME path returns a bare 404 on the pod host but a real DBMI error envelope on -ing. GET -> 405 'Request method GET is not supported' = the POST verb EXISTS. POST with an empty body -> 500 'Cannot invoke Object.getClass() because o is null' = the handler PARSED and RAN our request (a null-deref on a missing body, not a routing miss). Body shape still unknown - run the validator loop against this host.

| Business-entity EXISTENCE test (idiom) | Works: POST | Determine whether a business entity is deployed | THE reliable probe. POST .../entity/{be}?sourceSystem=X returns 404 'The requested metadata with GUID {be} cannot be fo… |

#### MCP coverage

| Action | Verb | Server | What it does | REST equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| search_master_record | POST | Customer Identification | Fuzzy identity match returning the business ID of the best-matching master record. | MCP ONLY. REST has no public MDM search or list resource. |
| get_master_record_details | POST | Customer Identification | The consolidated golden record, merged across source systems. | REST equivalent is the disputed GET on entity/{be}/{id}. MCP is the safer path. |

#### Caps that bite here

- **Job concurrency** — Queues ingress/egress past 25 per pod or 5 per org *(C360 p.247)*
- **Step queueing** — Load >1,000 rows; transform >100,000; index >10,000; match keys >5,000 *(C360 p.247)*
- **File and result caps** — CSV 100 MB / 100,000 rows; search page 10,000; export 10,000 *(C360 pp.65,168)*
- **Session** — Session ID expires after 30 min of inactivity *(vendor deck p.8)*

> **Mastering is entitled long before it is reachable.** This org holds 83 MDM privileges - full CRUD on mdm.asset.be, .srcsystem, .hierarchy, .relationship, .jobdef and .appmodel, plus execute.mdm.flows, manage.mdm.jobs and manage.mdm.schedules - and the login user holds MDM Designer and Customer 360 Data Steward/Manager/Analyst. None of that yields a deploy verb. Entitlement and reachability are separate questions: read privileges for the first, probe routes for the second.

> **P360 is not MDM SaaS. Do not answer a P360 question from this section.** Informatica MDM - Product 360 (P360) Cloud Edition is a separate AWS-hosted PIM with NO REST API. Deployment is triggered by uploading an empty do_deploy.txt marker file into an S3 customization folder; workflows deploy through the ActiveVOS console UI; DEV->QA->PROD promotion is a support ticket with a 4-hour window. Source: MDM Product 360 Cloud Edition Configuration and Customization Guide v10.0. A 'headless P360' answer means scripting S3 file drops, not calling an API.

> **The runtime plane is real even when every path 404s.** On a pod where data360/* returns fake-200s, the <pod>-mdm host still discriminates: GET entity/{be}/{id} -> 403 against a bogus twin's 404, and GET /rdm-service/external/v1/search -> 405 against 404. A 404 on that host is therefore 'wrong path', not 'no service'.

> **MDM job / flow / x360 planes: privileges without routes.** execute.mdm.flows, manage.mdm.jobs and view.mdm.x360 are all granted, yet 11 job/flow host+path shapes and 5 x360/config shapes all 404 on this pod. Holding a privilege does not imply the route is mounted - and mounting is per-pod, so this is UNTESTED elsewhere, not absent.

> ⚠️ **Open question.** MDM read-by-id: GET /business-entity/public/api/v1/entity/c360.person/{id} returned 200 in early-July testing but a later review concluded every MDM runtime path 404s under correct auth and the earlier 200s were identity-service login HTML. Re-probe and check the CONTENT TYPE, not just the status code.

> ⚠️ **Open question.** Is there any public search or list resource for golden records? Both reviews agree there is not, but the vendor deck documents a 'search' resource - confirm against the Business 360 REST API Reference.

> ⚠️ **Open question.** The B360 Modeler UI must call something to author a business entity. 12 public shapes are now excluded; the remaining hypothesis is a non-public/internal plane or a session-cookie-only endpoint. Capturing the browser network trace during one Publish would settle the biggest UNTESTED gap in this section.

> ⚠️ **Open question.** Whether a BUSINESS_ENTITY exported from another org imports cleanly into a pod holding zero MDM design objects. The import route is open (multipart) and export is proven elsewhere, but the cross-org retarget was never attempted end to end.

# MCP dictionary

Informatica publishes five managed MCP servers exposing eleven actions between them. This section is the consolidated view; the same actions also appear inside each service section next to that product's API table. Source: the official April-2026 Getting Started with Informatica MCP Servers guide.

### The five servers, and which IDMC product each one covers

| MCP server | Backing IDMC service | Actions | What it is for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Address Verification | Cloud Address Verification (CDQ) | 1 | Validate, standardize and geocode addresses in real time, 240+ countries |
| CDGC Metadata Search | CDGC catalog | 2 | Natural-language asset discovery; returns metadata including lineage and profile |
| Customer Identification | MDM SaaS / Customer 360 | 2 | Fuzzy identity resolution plus master (golden) record retrieval |
| Data Provisioning | Cloud Data Marketplace | 3 | List collections and targets, and raise a governed access request |
| Job Management | CDI execution engine | 3 | Trigger, monitor and stop mapping tasks in real time |

### All eleven actions across the five servers

| MCP action | Verb | Server | Key inputs | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| verify_address | POST | Address Verification | address payload | Validates, standardizes and geocodes an address; returns a validation status. Persists nothing. |
| search_metadata | POST | CDGC Metadata Search | knowledgeQuery (NL string) | Natural-language catalog query returning matching asset IDs and core attributes. |
| get_asset_details | POST | CDGC Metadata Search | id, scheme | Full metadata for one asset — includes lineage, profile and full descriptions. |
| search_master_record | POST | Customer Identification | customer details | Fuzzy match returning the business ID of the best-matching master record. |
| get_master_record_details | POST | Customer Identification | business ID | The consolidated golden record, merged across source systems. |
| list_data_collections | POST | Data Provisioning | limit, search | Lists marketplace data collections. |
| list_delivery_targets | POST | Data Provisioning | id (uuid), segments | Returns collection detail. Note: despite the name it does not return a target list. |
| checkout_data_order | POST | Data Provisioning | dataCollectionId, justification, targetRef | The only write in the catalog. Raises a formal access request; requires a business justification. |
| run_mapping_task | POST | Job Management | task plus runtime parameters | Triggers execution of a CDI mapping task. |
| get_job_status | POST | Job Management | job id | Live execution state, row counts and error logs. |
| stop_running_job | POST | Job Management | job id | Sends an immediate termination request to the Secure Agent. |

### Protocol and transport

| Property | Value | Note |
|---|---|---|
| MCP protocol version | 2025-06-18 | MCP guide p.7. Pin this when writing a client. |
| Transport | streamable HTTP | Not stdio. Remote servers, not local subprocesses. |
| Host / client model | your AI app = MCP host; each agent = MCP client; one client to one server | MCP guide p.6. Informatica calls MCP tools 'actions'; the details page says actions, third-party clients say tools. Same thing. |
| Where to see them | AI Agent Engineering > MCP Servers page | Each server's Configuration tab holds the endpoint URL and a paste-ready code block. |
| Supported clients | Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Python, and the AI Agent Engineering MCP Tool | MCP guide pp.13-14. |
| Metering | Not monetized during the AI Agent Engineering preview — BUT the underlying service APIs still bill IPUs at the service rate card | MCP guide p.7. The trap: MCP looks free, then CDGC, CDI, Marketplace and MDM calls appear on the bill. Budget the backing service, not the MCP layer. |

### Three ways to authenticate

| Method | Header to send | When to use it | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Session ID | headers={"IDS-SESSION-ID": "<session ID>"} | Quickest path; you already have this from a v1 login. | MCP guide pp.12-14. Same session ID the REST planes use. |
| JWT | headers={"Authorization": "Bearer <token>"} | When the org standardises on JWT. | Minted the same way as the data360 token. Remember the documented 30-minute lifetime. |
| OAuth — direct client | headers={"Authorization": "Bearer <token>"} | Production. The agent never holds a human user's IDMC credentials. | Client Credentials grant, POST to the token endpoint, OAuth 2.0. Recommended for anything long-lived. |
| OAuth — federated | headers={"Authorization": "Bearer <token>"} | Org uses SAML SSO; identity is delegated to Okta or Azure AD. | Requires the org configured for SAML with users set up as SAML users, plus a configured IdP. |

### OAuth client lifecycle — Configuration > MCP Server Authorization

| Operation | Where | What you get / must know |
|---|---|---|
| Add OAuth client | Add OAuth Client wizard: Authentication > Details > Resources > Generate Credentials | Returns client ID, client secret, and an auth header value (base64 of id:secret). On the Resources page you pick WHICH MCP servers this client may reach — scope it narrowly. |
| Access-token timeout | Details page of the wizard | Default 5 minutes. Range 5 to 1440 minutes (24 h). Five minutes will bite any long-running agent — raise it deliberately. |
| Secret retrieval | Generate Credentials page, once | The secret and header value are NOT available after the wizard closes. Copy them then, or regenerate. |
| Regenerate secret | Actions menu > Regenerate Secret | Re-authenticates with username and password first. The recovery path when a secret is lost. |
| Disable / enable | Actions menu > Disable or Enable | Enabled on creation. Disable stops token issuance without deleting — the correct response to a compromised client. |
| Edit | Edit icon | Change name, description, timeout, or which MCP servers are in scope. |
| Delete | Delete icon | For clients no longer needed. |
| Download report | Download CSV icon | Name, description, status, MCP servers and last-update date for every client. Ignores on-screen filters — always the full list. Useful as an audit artifact. |

### The CLAIRE MCP server in a Claude host — live enumeration

| Tool | Accepted arguments | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| OrchestratorSkill | prompt, conversation_id, name, external_id, artifacts, history, reasoning, events | General CLAIRE orchestration. One free-text prompt in, an artifact-bearing response out. |
| MdmOrchestratorSkill | prompt, conversation_id, name, external_id, artifacts, history, reasoning, events | The MDM-specialised twin. |
| new_conversation | (no domain args) | Must be called FIRST to obtain a conversation_id. Skipping it is the usual cause of a failed first call. |
| working | (NONE - takes no arguments at all) | Poll until the response is ready. CLAIRE is asynchronous - treat this as a poll-until-done loop. CORRECTED 2026-07-26 from the live tool schema: this action accepts NO arguments (properties={}), so d… |

### How many MCP servers are there, really

| Class | Count | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Informatica-MANAGED MCP servers | 5 - Address Verification, CDGC Metadata Search, Customer Identification, Data Provisioning, Job Management | AIAE April 2026 'Available MCP servers' p.7-8 enumerates exactly these five and no others. This is the authoritative catalog for that release. |
| ...of those, exposed on a probed org | 2 of 5 | GET /public/core/v3/mcpServers returned a populated registry on one org listing 2; the same path 404s on another org entirely. Exposure is per-org, not per-product. |
| CLAIRE / AI-agent MCP servers | separate class, NOT in the five | Reached at <claire_api_url>/claire-orchestrator-ai-agent/api/v1/mcp. Appears as tools in the HOST app, not in the org's mcpServers registry - so counting it against the five is a category error. |
| Your own / third-party servers | unbounded | Any MCP server you register in the host (claude mcp add) sits beside these. IDMC does not know about them. |
| Commonly-heard '5 to 10' | Treat as unverified | Only the 5 managed servers are vendor-enumerated for April 2026. If someone cites more, ask which RELEASE and whether they are counting AI-agent servers or their own registrations. Re-read the Availa… |

> **MCP is a small curated subset of REST, with two exceptions.** Seven of the eleven actions are thin wrappers over a REST endpoint you could call directly, and in several cases REST is strictly more capable - raw Elasticsearch DSL instead of one search string, 1,000 addresses per call instead of one, full job history instead of a single job. The two genuine exceptions are asset lineage via get_asset_details and fuzzy identity match via search_master_record; neither has any REST equivalent on this platform.

> **No MCP action authors a design-time asset.** There is no mapping designer, no rule authoring and no business-entity modelling in the MCP catalog. The read/write boundary is identical to REST's, which is the clearest evidence that MCP sits on top of the same service APIs rather than beside them.

> **Billing.** MCP server usage is not separately metered during the AI Agent Engineering preview, but the shared servers call IDMC service APIs underneath and that consumption incurs IPUs at your normal service rate card. Budget MCP as the underlying service.

> **Server availability is per-org.** Of the five published servers, a live enumeration of one lab tenant found only two exposed on its MCP host. The documented catalog is the ceiling, not a guarantee.

### REST or MCP — which to reach for

| Capability | Over REST | Over MCP | Which to use |
|---|---|---|---|
| Catalog search / asset detail | READ (data360 search + catalog) | READ — search_metadata, get_asset_details | MCP. Natural-language query is a real gain over building a query envelope. |
| Address validation / geocoding | READ (Cloud Address Verification) | READ — verify_address | Either. MCP is simpler for one address; REST batches 1,000. |
| Master-record lookup | MDM SaaS APIs (host-mounted, 404 on Org B) | READ — search_master_record, get_master_record_details | MCP. Fuzzy match is the whole value, and it is not trivial to replicate. |
| Marketplace order / provisioning | WRITE — full chain proven | WRITE — checkout_data_order (the only MCP write) | REST for the full chain; MCP for a conversational just-in-time request. |
| Run / monitor / stop a CDI task | RUN — v2 job, activityLog | EXECUTE — run_mapping_task, get_job_status, stop_running_job | Either. MCP is the cleaner surface for an operator agent. |
| Create a connection | WRITE — proven, §17 | no action | REST only. Nothing in MCP touches connections. |
| Publish CAI assets in bulk | RUN — asset/v1/publish, 199 max | no action | REST only. |
| CAI suspend / resume / terminate | RUN — restadmin, §16 | no action | REST only. Note Job Management MCP stops CDI jobs, not CAI instances. |
| Schedule anything | WRITE — v2 schedule + CAI restadmin scheduler | no action | REST only. |
| Users, groups, roles, agents | WRITE — v2 and v3 admin | no action | REST only. No MCP server fronts administration. |
| Glossary, classification accept, stewardship | UI-ONLY | no action | Neither. Still the most stubbornly UI-bound part of the platform. |

| CDGC write plane | same three-header flow | Bearer + IDS-SESSION-ID + X-INFA-ORG-ID | cdgc-api.dm-us.informaticacloud.com | ccgf-*, cdmp-marketplace |

## Status-code decoder

**Reading the response — what each code actually means**

| Code / error | What it actually means | Seen on |
|---|---|---|
| 404, empty body | The route is genuinely not mounted — a real UI-only wall | glossary, classification accept |
| 404, with a JSON or text body | Wrong path or wrong host — keep hunting | CAI publish: asset/publish vs asset/v1/publish |
| 405 Method not supported | Read-only resource. This is NOT an entitlement problem | POST /public/core/v3/objects |
| 403 | Missing service-account role, or an unregistered connector type | APP_105054, no connector with type |
| 406 | Business state — a job is already running for that source | re-firing a CDGC scan |
| 409 Conflict | Conflicts with the current state of the resource | CDQ dictionary operations |
| 413 Payload Too Large | You exceeded a documented cap | CDQ, more than 10,000 dictionary rows |
| 424 Failed Dependency | A prerequisite call was skipped | CDQ rows without finishUpload |
| 200 returning login HTML | You hit identity-service — wrong host or plane | profiling-service with INFA-SESSION-ID |
| 200 but the value reverts | Silent write rejection | mapping-task connection retarget |
| MigrationSvc_030 | Invalid import package — hand-built zips are rejected | v3 import |
| MigrationSvc_038 | 403 permission, not a missing route | v3 export (since granted) |
| APP_13533 | Specify a mapping ID — mttask only WRAPS an existing mapping | POST /api/v2/mttask |
| APP_13400 | Compute capacity exceeded | Fabric connection source fetch |
| exit 127 (agent side) | Native loader failure — a missing OS library | pmdtm and libidn.so.11 on Debian 12 |

**Add this row to the decoder ring**

| Code / signature | What it actually means | Seen on |
|---|---|---|
| 200, Content-Length: 0, NO Content-Type | Route is mounted at the gateway but nothing is serving behind it. NOT a success. Assert on body shape, never on status alone. | every data360 path on dmp-us (CDGC + Marketplace) |
| 200 {"count":0,"objects":[]} for a fabricated type | The v3 objects resource does NOT validate the type filter. q=type=='TOTALLY_FAKE_TYPE_ZZZ' returns the same clean empty result as a real type. An empty count is therefore never evidence that a featur… | GET /public/core/v3/objects?q=type=='...' |
| 415 Unsupported Media Type | Verb and path both exist; you sent the wrong Content-Type. Positive evidence, same family as 400/422. | GET /public/core/v3/runtimeEnvironment (singular) |

Enabling engines does NOT do this |

Clone backdoor also closed: POST /public/core/v3/import/package -> 404 MigrationSvc_025 | Business 360 Modeler -> Publish (one click). ## Documented caps

| Service | What is capped | The limit | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| CAI | Bulk publish / unpublish | 199 assets per call | Invoke ch.3-4 |
| CAI | Process list default page size | 20 (use listStart + maxReturn to page) | Monitor p.101 |
| CAI | Rate limit | HTTP 429 when requests exceed the window | Invoke p.12 |
| CAI | Activity execution circuit breaker | 10,000 activities -> 429, no new instances for 15 min (tech preview, node-local) | Invoke p.25 |
| CAI | Message payload | 5 MB on Cloud Server; 500 MB multi-byte ceiling | Monitor p.11 |
| CAI | Process timeout / retention | 3,600 s timeout; completed 24 h, faulted 72 h, logs 30 days | Invoke p.25 |
| CDQ | Dictionary shape | Name 125 chars; 42 columns max; column names 64 chars | CDQ API Ref p.7 |
| CDQ | Rows per call | 10,000 (POST and PUT) -> 413 if exceeded | CDQ API Ref p.11 |
| Address Verification | Batch size | 1,000 addresses per call; 100 suggestions interactive | IAV ch.2 |
| Address Verification | Job token | Expires in 5 min; free resubmit 2x interactive / 9x QuickCapture | IAV p.11 |
| Operational Insights | History + concurrency | 13 months (processJobReport), 1 month others; ONE active request per org | OI p.70 |
| Operational Insights | Data retention / refresh | 13 months retained; metrics refresh only once a week | OI p.70, p.110 |
| MDM SaaS | Job concurrency | Queues ingress/egress past 25 per pod or 5 per org | C360 p.247 |
| MDM SaaS | Step queueing | Load >1,000 rows; transform >100,000; index >10,000; match keys >5,000 | C360 p.247 |
| MDM SaaS | File and result caps | CSV 100 MB / 100,000 rows; search page 10,000; export 10,000 | C360 pp.65,168 |
| MDM SaaS | Session | Session ID expires after 30 min of inactivity | vendor deck p.8 |
| Data Profiling | Rule occurrences | Keep at 200 or fewer per profile | CDP p.160 |
| Platform | Token lifetime | JW access token expires 30 min after grant | IAV p.9 |
| MCP | OAuth token timeout | Default 5 min; configurable 5-1440 min | MCP guide |
